newsitem.title: UK: Independent Insurance profits up 46 percent.
newsitem.headline: Independent Insurance profits up 46 percent.

text.p: Independent Insurance Group Plc on Tuesday posted a 46 percent rise in full-year profits but warned that there were still few signs of an improvement in the UK insurance market.
Pre-tax profit including realised investment gains rose to 52.0 million stg from 35.5 million stg a year before and the full-year dividend was raised 18 percent to 13.25p from 11.25p.

Profits were reduced by a 2.1 million stg charge dictated by legal requirements, which came into force last year, for companies to take a provision to smooth earnings against adverse underwriting results.
Gross written premiums rose seven percent to 438.9 million stg from 410.5 million in 1995.
Chief executive Michael Bright said there had been little improvement so far in the competitive market conditions that he reported last year.

"I am disappointed to report that only now are there vague signs of increases in rates for certain classes of business," Bright said. "We are not immune to the problems of the insurance cycle, but sticking to our principles throughout this period has produced very gratifying results."
Bright said the current year had begun with a disappointing start to the property account, with continuing subsidence claims and poor weather.
However he said the group was experiencing real growth in the policy number count in its commercial operations for the first time in two years.
Bright added that the company would seek opportunities for acquisition as well as developing its existing business.
